title: Landlord Repairs or Improvements: What to Send Your Accountant
excerpt: A property invoice is not automatically an expense you can deduct from rental income. Repairs and capital improvements can have different tax treatment, and the description on the invoice may not tell the whole story.
metaTitle: Landlord Repairs vs Improvements: Evidence to Keep | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Repair or capital improvement? Prepare itemised property invoices, before-and-after details and purchase history so the tax treatment can be checked.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord shows before-and-after property repair photos and invoices to an accountant, spare tap on desk.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property

content:
A property invoice is not automatically an expense you can deduct from rental income. Repairs and capital improvements can have different tax treatment, and the description on the invoice may not tell the whole story.

Describe what changed

A repair generally restores something, while an improvement may add something beyond that. Give the accountant the before-and-after facts, not just a label such as “renovation”. Keep itemised invoices and explain whether several kinds of work were bundled into one bill.

For example, repairing storm damage and building a new extension are different projects. A replacement involving modern materials can need a more careful review than simply deciding that all new items are improvements.

Include the timing and property history

Explain when you bought the property, its condition at purchase and whether it was being let. Work before the first tenant or as part of a larger project may need particular attention.

Keep records even when a cost is not deducted from annual rental income. It may still be relevant to a later calculation, depending on the facts.

Do not force every invoice into one category

Ask the accountant whether parts of the work should be treated separately. A reasonable allocation needs evidence rather than a convenient percentage chosen at the end of the year.

Example: an itemised project

A single contractor invoice may include repairs, replacement items and an extension. Ask for a breakdown and explain the work, rather than entering the entire invoice under whichever category sounds most favourable.

Is a replacement always a repair?

Not automatically. The nature of the work, what was replaced and the broader circumstances need consideration. Modern materials do not by themselves answer every capital-versus-revenue question.

What if the cost is not deducted this year?

Keep the records anyway. A cost that is not an annual rental expense may be relevant to another calculation, depending on the circumstances. Do not discard invoices merely because they were excluded from this year’s rental-profit figure.

Next step: Share itemised invoices and a short description with TaxSimba before approving the property figures in your return.

Put it into practice

Split the project before choosing a tax category

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A contractor's £8,000 invoice covers roof repairs and a new extension. The landlord asks for an itemised breakdown, keeps photos and explains the property's condition and letting history. She does not claim the whole amount as repairs because one part repaired damage, or discard the capital part because it is not deducted from annual rent. The accountant reviews the work's substance and timing, including whether it forms part of a wider improvement project.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What was repaired, replaced or added?Provide before-and-after descriptions and itemised costs.
When and why was the work done?Explain purchase condition, letting status and any wider project.
Is part of the invoice capital?Keep that evidence for the appropriate future calculation rather than forcing it into annual expenses.

Two more questions you may have

Does a supplier calling work a repair settle the tax treatment?

No. The actual work and circumstances matter. Give the accountant enough detail to assess them.

Do modern replacement materials automatically mean improvement?

No. A modern equivalent can require a more nuanced assessment. Describe what changed in function, capacity and quality.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect itemised invoices and payment records.
  • Describe what existed before and after.
  • Record purchase and letting history.
  • Identify wider projects and mixed invoices.
  • Retain capital-cost evidence separately.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Savings Interest: When Do You Need to Tell HMRC or File a Return?
excerpt: Tax on savings interest does not always mean you need to purchase a Self Assessment service. Start by checking how HMRC expects your particular income to be reported.
metaTitle: Savings Interest: Self Assessment or Another Route? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Add savings interest across accounts, check joint ownership and tax-free accounts, then confirm whether HMRC needs a return or can collect tax another way.
featuredImageAlt: A saver gathers interest statements from several banks beside a separate ISA folder and accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax on savings interest: How you pay tax on savings interest
GOV.UK — Check how much tax you pay on dividends and interest from savings

content:
Tax on savings interest does not always mean you need to purchase a Self Assessment service. Start by checking how HMRC expects your particular income to be reported.

Add up the relevant interest

Gather annual interest statements from the accounts concerned, including accounts you closed. Use the tax year, not an arbitrary twelve-month period. Tell the accountant about joint accounts and different types of savings rather than assuming every payment has the same treatment.

HMRC’s current guidance explains the allowances and reporting routes. If you already complete Self Assessment, savings interest should be included in the return as required. People outside Self Assessment may have tax collected another way.

Do not infer the position from one bank

Several small amounts can add up, while income and tax bands can affect the calculation. An account being described as a savings account does not mean all interest is exempt. Explain any tax-free account status to the accountant.

Check before buying

Use HMRC’s guidance or ask for the filing requirement to be confirmed. If the only issue can be dealt with without a return, do not assume a full SA engagement is necessary.

Example: several accounts

If interest comes from three banks, prepare one schedule showing each institution and the relevant annual amount. Include closed accounts. Do not use only the balance shown in your main banking app.

Is all interest tax-free because I have an allowance?

Not necessarily. Allowances depend on the person’s wider position and the type of income or account. A return may need the information even where the resulting tax on some interest is nil.

If the bank reports interest, why tell the accountant?

The return still needs to be complete. Give the accountant the statements and explain any joint-account share. A change in a PAYE tax code should also be checked rather than assumed to match the correct year’s final liability.

Next step: Share the relevant interest statements and other income details with TaxSimba if you need a return or want the position reviewed within an agreed service.

Put it into practice

Three modest accounts still need one total

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Nora receives £240, £310 and £180 interest from three ordinary savings accounts during the tax year, including an account she closed. She totals £730 and keeps the annual certificates, with ISA interest identified separately. Whether tax is due depends on her wider income and available allowances; whether a return is needed is another question. If she already files, she provides the interest information rather than assuming the banks' reporting completes her return.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Do the figures cover the UK tax year?Use annual statements and include closed accounts.
Are any accounts joint or tax-free?Record the account type and relevant ownership share.
Is Self Assessment actually required?Check current HMRC reporting rules alongside other income and any notice to file.

Two more questions you may have

Does every interest-tax bill require Self Assessment?

No. HMRC may collect tax another way depending on the facts. Check before purchasing an annual-return service solely for interest.

Can I ignore interest below an allowance when I already file?

Give the accountant the relevant statements so the return and allowance calculation can be completed correctly.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • List all accounts, including closed ones.
  • Collect interest certificates for the tax year.
  • Identify joint-account shares and ISAs.
  • List other income affecting allowance calculations.
  • Check HMRC's required reporting or collection route.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Working from Home When Self-Employed: Preparing an Expense Claim
excerpt: Working from home can involve allowable business costs, but the whole household bill does not become deductible. The useful starting point is a clear explanation of how the home is used for work.
metaTitle: Working from Home: Self-Employed Expense Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare a supported working-from-home claim with household bills, working hours and mixed-use details, and compare actual costs with simplified expenses.
featuredImageAlt: A freelancer measures home workspace use with a planner, utility bills and laptop, cosy apartment setting.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Office, property and equipment

content:
Working from home can involve allowable business costs, but the whole household bill does not become deductible. The useful starting point is a clear explanation of how the home is used for work.

Gather the facts before choosing a method

Tell your accountant which activities take place at home, how much time they take and what space is used. Keep relevant bills and explain whether rooms have both business and personal use.

HMRC permits an appropriate business allocation for certain home costs. Simplified-expense rules may also be relevant. Ask which approach is suitable rather than choosing a convenient percentage without evidence.

Keep phone and internet claims separate enough to understand

A shared connection or mobile plan needs consideration of private use. Paying the bill from a business account does not by itself establish that the whole cost relates to work.

Avoid unsupported calculations

A spreadsheet showing the calculation is useful when it connects back to bills and a reasonable method. Keep the explanation with the figures so it can be reviewed next year.

If you use part of the property exclusively for business or are considering significant changes to the arrangement, ask about wider consequences before acting. A routine expense claim should not accidentally become a property-tax planning decision.

Example: a room used for work and family life

Explain the hours and nature of business use, keep the bills and show the proposed allocation. The fact that a desk is in a room does not make every household cost a business expense.

Can I add a flat-rate claim to all the actual household costs?

Do not assume the methods can be stacked. Ask which costs the chosen approach covers and what needs separate consideration. Keep phone and internet treatment clear enough to avoid duplication.

What if the working pattern changes?

Update the explanation rather than automatically carrying forward last year’s percentage. Moving home, renting a workspace or reducing hours can change the evidence behind the calculation. The accountant should be able to follow the method from records rather than reconstruct it from memory.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the relevant bills and a short description of your working pattern. Your accountant can review the allowable amount as part of the agreed work.

Put it into practice

A desk does not make the whole household bill deductible

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A consultant uses a family room for client work on some weekdays and for personal use at other times. She records the working pattern and gathers relevant household bills. Her accountant compares an appropriate actual-cost allocation with any available simplified method, checking what each covers. She keeps phone and internet treatment clear and avoids adding a full household-cost claim to a flat-rate amount for the same costs. She updates the calculation after changing her work routine.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
How is the home used for the business?Describe activities, space, hours and shared personal use.
Which calculation method fits?Compare the permitted methods using actual evidence and avoid overlapping deductions.
Has the arrangement changed?Update the basis after a move, new workspace or substantial change in working hours.

Two more questions you may have

Can I claim all rent or mortgage payments because I work at home?

No. The type of cost and reasonable business allocation need checking. Loan capital repayments do not become business expenses.

Is exclusive business use always preferable?

It can have wider consequences. Explain the actual use and seek advice before making property-use decisions solely for a deduction.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Describe the home-based activities.
  • Record working hours and shared room use.
  • Collect relevant household bills.
  • Keep phone and internet use identifiable.
  • Document the chosen method and any changed circumstances.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Mileage or Actual Vehicle Costs: Which Records Does Your Accountant Need?
excerpt: Mileage and actual-cost methods are not two allowances to add together. Before preparing a vehicle claim, your accountant needs to know which method is available and what has been claimed before.
metaTitle: Self-Employed Mileage vs Actual Vehicle Costs | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare vehicle claim methods using journey records, purchase history and private-use details, and avoid claiming mileage plus the same running costs.
featuredImageAlt: A self-employed person compares mileage log with actual vehicle invoices and business-use notes, car outside.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Vehicles
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Car, van and travel expenses

content:
Mileage and actual-cost methods are not two allowances to add together. Before preparing a vehicle claim, your accountant needs to know which method is available and what has been claimed before.

Keep both the business facts and the vehicle history

Provide the vehicle type, purchase or lease details, business use and any private use. Tell the accountant about previous capital allowances or deductions. Prior treatment can restrict simplified mileage claims.

A mileage record should show enough detail to explain the business journeys. Receipts remain useful for reviewing actual costs and other relevant expenses. Travel between home and a normal workplace needs particular care.

Do not decide from fuel spending alone

Fuel is only one part of a vehicle’s cost, and a flat-rate method is not calculated by simply reimbursing fuel receipts. The accountant should compare the relevant evidence and rules for the tax year.

If you use several vehicles, identify them separately. Avoid combining miles and costs in one total with no explanation of which vehicle was used.

Choose consistently and keep the evidence

Ask how the selected method affects later years before switching. A method that appears attractive for one period may not be freely changeable afterwards.

Example: one cost, two possible approaches

A vehicle used for business and privately needs a method that fits the rules and its history. A mileage calculation and fuel receipts may help a comparison, but they are not automatically two deductions for the same journeys.

Can I switch methods whenever the result looks better?

Do not assume so. Previous claims and rules for the vehicle can restrict the options. Give the accountant earlier calculations before changing anything.

What does a useful journey record include?

Keep dates, business purpose and mileage in a consistent form. Explain the start and end points where needed. An annual total with no supporting trail can be difficult to review, especially where normal commuting and business travel have been mixed together.

Next step: Give TaxSimba your mileage evidence, vehicle documents and previous return calculations so the treatment can be reviewed before the figures are approved.

Put it into practice

Prepare both evidence sets without claiming both

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A self-employed tutor logs 2,400 business miles with dates, destinations and purposes. She also retains vehicle purchase records, insurance and running-cost receipts. Her accountant checks which method is available, what previous claims were made and which journeys qualify. Keeping both evidence sets helps the review; it does not mean she can add a mileage deduction to all fuel, repair and insurance costs for the same vehicle. Private journeys and ordinary commuting are identified separately.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Is the journey genuinely business travel?Record purpose and route; distinguish normal commuting and personal use.
What has been claimed for this vehicle before?Provide prior expense and capital-allowance calculations before considering a switch.
Would the claim duplicate running costs?Apply the chosen method consistently and check any separately permitted items.

Two more questions you may have

Can I switch methods every year to whichever is larger?

Not necessarily. The vehicle's history and the method's rules can restrict later choices. Check before changing.

Is fuel spending enough to prove business mileage?

No. Keep a journey log and business purpose. Fuel receipts alone do not establish which miles qualify.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • List each vehicle and acquisition details.
  • Keep dated business journey logs.
  • Record private use and commuting separately.
  • Collect actual running-cost evidence.
  • Locate earlier claims and confirm the available method.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: SA302 and Tax-Year Overview: Evidence for a Mortgage Application
excerpt: A mortgage lender may ask for a tax calculation and tax-year overview as evidence of self-employed income. These are related documents, but they are not the same thing as a bank statement or a promise that a loan will be approved.
metaTitle: SA302 and Tax-Year Overview: Mortgage Evidence | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare the tax calculation and tax-year overview your lender requests, check the correct years and versions, and distinguish drafts from filed records.
featuredImageAlt: A mortgage applicant and adviser compare tax calculation and tax-year overview papers beside house keys.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Get your SA302 tax calculation
GOV.UK — Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Tax calculation (SA302)

content:
A mortgage lender may ask for a tax calculation and tax-year overview as evidence of self-employed income. These are related documents, but they are not the same thing as a bank statement or a promise that a loan will be approved.

Ask the lender exactly what it needs

Confirm the years, document format and any other requirements. HMRC explains how to obtain your SA302 tax calculation and tax-year overview, including where returns were filed using software.

A lender can have its own process. Do not assume a document accepted by one lender will be sufficient for every application.

Make sure the figures relate to the right return

Check your name, tax year and whether the return has been submitted or subsequently amended. If you have only draft figures, describe them accurately rather than presenting them as completed HMRC records.

Ask the accountant how the calculation relates to the return and whether an updated document is needed after a correction.

Keep tax preparation separate from borrowing advice

An accountant should prepare accurate figures based on the records, not change income to meet a mortgage target. The lender decides affordability and eligibility. Filing a return does not guarantee a mortgage or an immediate document turnaround.

Before requesting documents

Ask the lender or broker which years and formats it requires, then tell the accountant exactly what was requested. A tax calculation and a tax-year overview should not be treated as interchangeable simply because both mention the same year.

Can an accountant create documents before filing?

An accountant can explain the stage reached and may prepare draft calculations, but those should not be represented as a submitted return or HMRC-generated overview. Use accurate labels and check the lender’s requirements.

What if a return was amended?

Tell the person handling the application. The latest calculation may differ from an earlier copy. Keep the version and relevant tax year clear, and ask whether the supporting overview also needs refreshing before documents are sent.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba what the lender requested and the relevant tax years so the team can confirm the documents and work it can provide.

Put it into practice

Match the documents to the lender's request

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A broker asks for two years of tax calculations and matching tax-year overviews. Dan confirms the exact years and accepted format, then checks that each calculation relates to the submitted return and that an amendment has been reflected. He does not send a draft labelled as a final HMRC record. Accurate tax evidence supports the application, but the lender still decides affordability and can ask for other documents or explanations.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Which years and formats are required?Obtain the lender or broker's exact document request.
Are the return versions current?Check filing and amendment status before downloading or requesting copies.
Do calculations and overviews match?Keep names, tax years and versions consistent across the pack.

Two more questions you may have

Are an SA302 and a tax-year overview interchangeable?

No. They show related but different information. Supply what the lender actually requests.

Can higher income be inserted to help a mortgage application?

No. The return must reflect supported figures. Lending goals do not justify changing the tax facts.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Confirm the lender's requested years and formats.
  • Check that relevant returns are filed.
  • Identify amendments and current calculations.
  • Obtain matching tax-year overviews.
  • Review the pack for names, years and consistency.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: High Salary Alone: Do You Actually Need Self Assessment?
excerpt: A high salary is not a reliable stand-alone rule for deciding whether you need Self Assessment. Filing rules have changed, and the relevant tax year and other circumstances matter.
metaTitle: High Salary: Do You Need Self Assessment? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check current Self Assessment filing rules for high earners, review other income and deal with any HMRC notice rather than relying on old salary thresholds.
featuredImageAlt: A high-salary employee reviews a payslip and other-income checklist with an accountant, no assumption of automatic return.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return
GOV.UK — Complete your Self Assessment tax return for the last tax year

content:
A high salary is not a reliable stand-alone rule for deciding whether you need Self Assessment. Filing rules have changed, and the relevant tax year and other circumstances matter.

Use the current HMRC check

Do not rely on an old article that says everyone above a particular employment-income figure must file. HMRC’s current checker considers the tax year and reasons a return may be needed. If HMRC has issued a notice to file, address it rather than ignoring it because of a general rule you read online.

Review income beyond the payslip

Tell the accountant about rental income, self-employment, savings, dividends and disposals. Pension contributions, benefits and other circumstances may also need review. An employer deducting PAYE does not mean every part of your wider position has been dealt with.

Separate a filing requirement from an advice need

Someone may want help checking a tax position without necessarily needing a full annual return. Equally, a return may still be needed for a reason unrelated to salary. Ask what service is appropriate before paying.

Avoid assuming that every high earner is eligible for a refund or that a pension payment will automatically solve the issue.

Example: salary plus another income source

Two people with the same employment salary may have different filing requirements if one also has rental income, dividends or taxable disposals. The salary figure alone cannot establish that their tax administration is identical.

Should I ignore a notice to file if I think no return is needed?

No. Contact HMRC or ask the accountant to deal with the notice appropriately. Reading a general exception is not the same as having an issued filing requirement withdrawn.

Can I still ask for a review without a mandatory return?

Yes, subject to the provider offering and agreeing that work. Be clear whether you need a filing service, a check of a particular issue or broader advice. Avoid paying for a return purely because an outdated threshold article told you every high earner must file.

Next step: Check HMRC’s current tool and explain your complete circumstances to TaxSimba so the required work can be confirmed.

Put it into practice

Same salary, different filing facts

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Two employees earn the same salary through PAYE. One has only employment income; the other also runs a trade and receives rent. They use HMRC's current checker for the relevant year rather than assuming the same salary creates the same filing requirement. Each checks benefits, interest, dividends and any notice to file. A personal tax review may still be useful without a mandatory return, but the service should fit the actual issue.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Which tax year and current filing rules apply?Use HMRC's current checker rather than an old high-income threshold article.
Is there income beyond PAYE?List trading, property, savings, dividends and relevant disposals.
Has HMRC issued a notice to file?Address the notice and seek withdrawal where appropriate instead of simply ignoring it.

Two more questions you may have

Does PAYE prove all my tax is settled?

No. PAYE deductions may not cover separate income, benefits or every adjustment in your wider position.

Should I buy a return service solely because my salary is high?

First confirm the filing requirement and the issue you need reviewed. An advice need and a return requirement are different questions.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Identify the tax year.
  • Use the current HMRC filing checker.
  • List income and benefits beyond salary.
  • Review any notice to file.
  • Agree whether you need filing or a specific tax review.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Lost Receipts Before Your Tax Return? What to Do Next
excerpt: Missing receipts do not justify inventing expenses or ignoring the tax return. Start rebuilding the evidence and tell your accountant what is missing as early as possible.
metaTitle: Lost Receipts Before Self Assessment: Rebuild Evidence | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Missing tax records? Request duplicates, reconstruct transactions and distinguish estimated from provisional figures before approving your return.
featuredImageAlt: A trader reconstructs a missing receipt using bank evidence, supplier email and diary notes; no fake documents.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: How long to keep your records

content:
Missing receipts do not justify inventing expenses or ignoring the tax return. Start rebuilding the evidence and tell your accountant what is missing as early as possible.

Try to replace the records

Ask suppliers for duplicate invoices, download bank statements and search email accounts or booking systems. Keep the reconstructed evidence in one place. A bank payment can help identify a transaction, but may not explain exactly what was bought or whether it was for business.

Mark what is uncertain

Prepare a list of missing items with the date, amount and explanation. Distinguish a figure you expect to confirm later from one that cannot be fully verified. Your accountant needs that distinction to consider how the return should describe the figures.

HMRC has guidance for estimated and provisional figures where records cannot be replaced. The return may need an explanation, and provisional figures need updating when actual figures become available.

Do not hide the problem until approval

The accountant should know the evidence limits before presenting the return for your review. Ask what can be supported, what needs more work and whether anything should be excluded.

Improve the routine afterwards

Capture documents regularly and check that uploads are readable. A photo of a receipt is only useful if it shows the relevant details.

Example: a supplier invoice is missing

A bank payment and order email can help identify the transaction. Ask the supplier for a duplicate and give the accountant the evidence available. Do not create a substitute receipt that pretends to be the original.

Is a round-number estimate acceptable by default?

No. Try to reconstruct actual figures first. If that cannot be done, tell the accountant why and keep the working behind any estimate. The appropriate disclosure and treatment depend on the circumstances.

What if I later find the document?

Tell the accountant whether the return has been submitted and how the confirmed amount compares with the figure used. A provisional amount is not meant to remain untouched once the actual information becomes available.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the records you have and a clear missing-record list, so the accountant can assess the next steps without guessing.

Put it into practice

A payment trail can help recover the invoice

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A sole trader finds a £185 business-account payment but no receipt. She locates an order email and asks the supplier for a duplicate, then explains the purchase's business purpose and any private use. She records unresolved items on a missing-evidence schedule instead of creating replacement receipts herself. Where actual records cannot be recovered, the accountant considers HMRC's requirements for estimates or provisional figures and any explanation or later update needed.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Can the original evidence be replaced?Request supplier copies and recover bank, email or platform records first.
What exactly remains uncertain?List the date, amount, purpose and evidence gap for each item.
Is the figure estimated or awaiting confirmation?Agree the appropriate disclosure and follow-up rather than leaving a provisional figure indefinitely.

Two more questions you may have

Does a bank payment guarantee an expense claim?

No. It may not establish the item, business purpose or private-use split. Provide all available supporting context.

What if I find the receipt after filing?

Compare it with the amount used and tell the accountant. A correction or update may be needed depending on the difference and how the return was completed.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Make a transaction-level missing-record list.
  • Request supplier or platform duplicates.
  • Recover bank and email evidence.
  • Document the basis of any unavoidable estimate.
  • Track provisional figures until actual amounts are known.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Child Benefit and Self Assessment: Check Whether PAYE Is an Option
excerpt: A High Income Child Benefit Charge does not always mean you need Self Assessment solely for that charge. HMRC now provides a PAYE route where the qualifying conditions are met.
metaTitle: Child Benefit Charge: PAYE or Self Assessment? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check whether the High Income Child Benefit Charge can be paid through PAYE, confirm the tax year and consider other reasons you may still need a return.
featuredImageAlt: A parent checks Child Benefit letters and PAYE records with an adviser, family photo and careful paperwork.

sources.label: GOV.UK — High Income Child Benefit Charge: Pay the tax charge through PAYE
GOV.UK — Personal Allowances: adjusted net income
GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return

content:
A High Income Child Benefit Charge does not always mean you need Self Assessment solely for that charge. HMRC now provides a PAYE route where the qualifying conditions are met.

Check the conditions before paying for a return

The PAYE option can apply when you do not need a return for another reason, are paying for the relevant current or previous year and act within HMRC’s permitted timeframe. For 2025/26, the guidance gives 31 January 2027 as the relevant cut-off for this option.

If you have self-employment or another reason to file, the position can be different. Use HMRC’s current guidance rather than assuming the charge is the only issue.

Bring the household facts

Tell the accountant who received Child Benefit, the relevant dates and the income information needed to assess the charge. Adjusted net income is not always the same as salary or the amount paid into your bank.

Do not simply stop filing

If you have previously filed only because of the charge, HMRC explains how to contact it about leaving Self Assessment and registering for PAYE collection instead. Do not ignore an outstanding notice to file.

A useful distinction

Child Benefit received, the person responsible for any charge and the method of paying that charge are separate questions. Give the accountant the household and income facts rather than assuming the recipient alone must always file.

Does PAYE collection deal with my other income?

Not automatically. A PAYE route for this charge does not settle separate self-employment, rental or other reporting requirements. Check the complete position before deciding that no return is needed.

What if I have already received a filing notice?

Address it with HMRC. Do not stop filing without checking the steps needed to leave Self Assessment where appropriate. Keep confirmation of the arrangement and review it if circumstances change. The availability of a route can also depend on the year and timing.

Next step: Check the current HMRC conditions first. If you need a return for other income or want the wider position reviewed, explain that to TaxSimba before choosing a package.

Put it into practice

The collection route follows the complete circumstances

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A parent needs to address the Child Benefit charge for 2025/26. She gathers both partners' relevant income details, Child Benefit dates and pension information, then checks whether HMRC's PAYE route is available within the permitted timeframe. If separate rental or trading income requires a return, that changes the filing question. If HMRC has already issued a notice to file, she arranges the correct action rather than assuming a PAYE request cancels it.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Who is responsible for the charge?Check the relevant household facts and adjusted net income, not only who receives the payments.
Does the PAYE route fit the year and timing?Use HMRC's current conditions before choosing collection through a tax code.
Is a return required for another reason?Review all income and deal with any existing filing notice.

Two more questions you may have

Does the benefit recipient always pay the charge?

Not necessarily. Responsibility depends on the applicable household and income rules. Supply both partners' relevant details.

Can I stop filing once I request PAYE collection?

Do not assume so. Follow HMRC's process for any existing return requirement and retain confirmation.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Record Child Benefit recipients and dates.
  • Gather both partners' relevant income information.
  • Identify pension and Gift Aid details affecting adjusted net income.
  • Check PAYE-route timing and eligibility.
  • Resolve other filing reasons and existing notices.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Pension Contributions and Adjusted Net Income: What to Tell Your Accountant
excerpt: Pension contributions can affect a tax calculation, but the accountant needs to know how the contributions were made. A total described simply as “my pension payments” may not be enough.
metaTitle: Pensions and Adjusted Net Income: Avoid Double Relief | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare pension contribution records by tax year and method, distinguish relief at source from payroll treatment and avoid claiming the same relief twice.
featuredImageAlt: A professional brings pension contribution evidence and payslips to an accountant, retirement planning scrapbook.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Claim tax relief on your private pension payments
GOV.UK — Personal Allowances: adjusted net income

content:
Pension contributions can affect a tax calculation, but the accountant needs to know how the contributions were made. A total described simply as “my pension payments” may not be enough.

Identify the contribution method

Gather pension statements and relevant payslips. Explain whether contributions came from pay, were paid personally or involved salary sacrifice. Different tax-relief methods mean the same-looking payment should not automatically be entered in the same place.

HMRC’s guidance explains the treatment of relief-at-source contributions and claims for additional relief. Avoid claiming relief twice where it has already been given through another mechanism.

Explain the wider income picture

Adjusted net income can matter for the Personal Allowance and other income-related rules. The accountant needs the relevant income and contribution details, not only your headline salary.

Timing is important. Identify the date contributions were paid and the tax year concerned. Do not assume a payment made now can retrospectively fix the previous year’s position.

Get advice before making a large payment

Tax treatment, contribution limits and the suitability of a pension decision need their own review. A tax-return article is not a recommendation to invest or transfer money.

Example: a personal contribution statement

If you made a payment personally, provide the statement showing the contribution and any tax relief added by the provider. Do not enter the same contribution again as though it were a separate payroll deduction.

Can I claim additional relief automatically?

The answer depends on the contribution method, income and relevant limits. Basic-rate relief already added by a provider does not settle every higher-rate claim, but it must be accounted for to avoid duplication.

Can I backdate a contribution by changing the description?

No. Give the accountant the actual payment dates. Ask about the rules before making decisions; allowances or carry-forward concepts do not mean a new payment can simply be described as paid in an earlier tax year.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the pension documents and explain what you want checked. The accountant can review the tax-return treatment within the agreed scope and identify where separate specialist advice is needed.

Put it into practice

The provider's top-up is part of the record

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A pension statement shows a personal net payment of £800 and £200 basic-rate relief added by the provider, giving £1,000 gross under relief at source. The taxpayer supplies that statement and the payment date rather than describing the £800 and £1,000 as two separate contributions. Payroll deductions and salary sacrifice are listed separately. Any additional relief and adjusted-net-income effect depend on the wider circumstances and limits; the example is not a recommendation to contribute.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
How was the contribution made?Identify relief at source, net pay, salary sacrifice or another arrangement.
Which tax year received the payment?Use actual payment dates and provider evidence.
Has relief already been given elsewhere?Reconcile payroll and provider records before entering a claim.

Two more questions you may have

Can a payment made now be backdated to last year?

Do not relabel the date. Carry-forward concepts do not make a new contribution a payment in an earlier tax year.

Does basic-rate relief mean no further action is ever needed?

Not necessarily. Additional relief can depend on the method and tax position. Have the evidence checked without duplicating relief already given.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect provider statements and payslips.
  • Identify the contribution and relief method.
  • Record net, relief and gross amounts correctly.
  • Allocate payments to the actual tax year.
  • Flag limits or large contributions for a separate review.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Crypto Swaps and Tax: Why Not Cashing Out Does Not Settle the Question
excerpt: Keeping money inside a crypto exchange does not automatically mean there is no tax event. Exchanging one token for another can require a Capital Gains Tax calculation even when no pounds reach your bank.
metaTitle: Crypto Swaps and Tax: No Cash Withdrawal Needed | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Crypto-to-crypto exchanges can be disposals. Prepare exchange and wallet histories, distinguish own-wallet transfers and check income events separately.
featuredImageAlt: A crypto user records an exchange between two abstract token symbols on laptop and preserves transaction history, no coin logos.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Check if you need to pay tax when you sell cryptoassets
GOV.UK — CRYPTO10400 - Introduction to cryptoassets: record keeping - HMRC internal manual

content:
Keeping money inside a crypto exchange does not automatically mean there is no tax event. Exchanging one token for another can require a Capital Gains Tax calculation even when no pounds reach your bank.

Reconstruct the transactions, not just the balance

Keep exports from every exchange and wallet involved. Record transfers clearly so moving assets between your own wallets is not confused with a sale. The accountant needs dates, quantities, values and relevant costs to understand the sequence.

HMRC identifies sales, exchanges and certain other disposals as events that may give rise to a gain. A later fall in the portfolio value does not, by itself, explain the tax treatment of an earlier disposal.

Separate income events from later disposals

Tokens received through certain activities can raise different tax questions from tokens simply bought and held. Tell the accountant about staking, rewards or payments received rather than including only trades against pounds.

Check the specialist work before purchasing

Large transaction histories, missing records and complex products can require additional calculations. Do not assume a standard SA package includes unlimited crypto reconciliation or every specialist issue.

Export records while access is available. An exchange balance today is not a substitute for the historical evidence needed for the return.

Example: a token-to-token exchange

A person exchanges one cryptoasset for another and keeps everything on the platform. No pounds are withdrawn, but the exchange can still be a disposal needing calculation. Later movements in the new asset’s value are a separate part of the history.

Is the platform’s profit figure enough?

Not always. Transfers, holdings on other exchanges and earlier acquisition records can affect the calculation. Keep exports and explain gaps rather than assuming one dashboard captures the whole history.

Does a loss mean there is nothing to report?

Do not decide solely from the current portfolio balance. Ask the accountant about realised transactions and any relevant reporting or loss claims. Confirm specialist support and the fee before commissioning a large reconciliation; a standard annual-return package should not be assumed to cover every crypto product.

Next step: Ask TaxSimba to confirm whether the crypto work can be supported, what records are required and the agreed fee before proceeding.

Put it into practice

A swap can matter before any pounds are withdrawn

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A taxpayer exchanges one token for another when the first token has risen in value. He keeps the time, quantity, sterling value, fees and acquisition history for the swap, even though no money reaches his bank. He identifies transfers between his own wallets so they are not treated as sales by mistake, and flags staking receipts separately. The final gain needs the relevant matching and pooling rules; today's portfolio balance cannot replace the historical calculation.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What was sold, swapped or spent?Build a disposal history with dates, quantities, sterling values and relevant costs.
Which movements are your own-wallet transfers?Link the sending and receiving records to prevent duplicate or false disposals.
Were tokens received as income?Identify rewards, payments and other receipts separately for tax review.

Two more questions you may have

Does keeping assets on an exchange prevent tax?

No. A disposal can occur without withdrawing pounds. The transaction type and facts matter.

Can one platform's profit figure cover everything?

Not necessarily. Holdings and transactions elsewhere, missing acquisition costs and UK matching rules can change the calculation.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Export all exchange and wallet histories.
  • Identify acquisitions, swaps, sales and spending.
  • Link own-wallet transfers.
  • Record rewards and other income events separately.
  • Agree specialist calculation scope before commissioning work.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.
